subject: Cleaner and better code with the backpipe package

messages.author: bb28a95def3e16fb
messages.subject: Cleaner and better code with the backpipe package
parts:
Hi all,

I have wrote the backpipe package that I believe will make Shiny code more readable, more debuggable, more maintainable and clearer.  If you love magrittr and pipeR, you may have been frustrated using it to write shiny code. Let's say you are doing something like this: 

     h1( "content", role="heading" )        %>%
       div( class="inner")                  %>%
          div( class="outer")                %>% 
             div( class="outer-outer")

This produces valid HTML:


    <div class="outer-outer">
      <div class="outer">
        <div class="inner">
           <h1 role="heading">content</h1>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

but illustrates two incongruities between code and output. The First is the reversal of order between code and output. This makes it hard to debug the generated HTML. The second problems is that code indentation no longer illustrate the nested structure of the output. Using the backpipe operator the same code can be written as:


        

    library(backpipe)
    
    div( class="outer-outer")               %<%
       div( class="outer")                  %<% 
         div( class="inner")                %<% 
           h1( "content", role="heading" )

Now operation order and code better matches the generated HTML output.


I hope this helps for the larger Shiny projects.  I would appreciate any feedback you have.

Thanks,

Chris

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Re: Cleaner and better code with the backpipe package
parts:
Nice idea, thank you.

My first reaction when I was reading your text was "I never use or seen people use magirttr pipes in shiny code".  I suppose the reason I never even thought of doing it is because of how you have to write the HTML backwards as you mentioned.

It would help if you maybe also compare the native Shiny way of writing the same code

div(class="outer-outer",
  div(class="outer",
    div(class="inner",
h1("content", role="heading")

)
  )
)

It's easier to compare this version to your backpipe version, and every Shiny developer understands this code. It honestly took me a minute to understand the magrittr version.
